observed: The old job becomes killed around the original five-second deadline. The second job is already registered before that and remains running until the new task independently reaches its 20-second deadline; its tool result then reports AbortError. The log does not establish where the PowerShell process was waiting.
hypothesis: Parallel non-interactive Windows PowerShell jobs share a module-analysis cache that is written asynchronously. Test the documented NUL cache opt-out in each managed shell process. The macOS PowerShell Core issue is only a related hypothesis, not proof of this Windows 5.1 failure.
unchanged_assertions: original task five seconds / old sleep eight seconds
new task twenty seconds / new sleep six seconds / foreground wait thirty seconds
old file absent and independent new file present
same SDK host process retained and provider request count unchanged
status_boundary: Do not claim the cache is the cause or that native command deadlines are accepted until the unchanged source and bundled SDK methods pass.
intervention_result: Same independent follow-up remains running until its own 20-second deadline; NUL module-cache opt-out did not remove the failure.

next_diagnostic.scope: Source-only probe passed, followed by the complete matrix acceptance in full_revalidation.

focused_bootstrap_failure.reason: Dedicated diagnostic workflow did not export MEDAGENT_PYTHON before the isolation probe; original full matrix exports it through windows.ps1. Corrected in 014ed2a.

entry_timing_result.interpretation: The new script enters about 1.5 seconds after its task starts but does not reach the post-Start-Sleep marker before its own 20-second deadline. This excludes slow command entry as the sole explanation, but does not prove whether module discovery or the cmdlet wait is responsible.

utility_import_result.scope: Native isolation probe and one source SDK deadline method with both independent_followup=False/True subcases. Normal matrix job was skipped by explicit diagnostic input. Not full Windows acceptance.
utility_import_result.interpretation: Explicitly importing the built-in Utility module before workspace command discovery removes the reproducible failure in this focused run. This supports the initialization fix but is not a trace of the internal Windows module-discovery hang.
